builds.titulo: Ocarina of Time looks clean on the phone

cambios.texto: Satronho NX's own fix: in Ocarina of Time the game's picture was full of horizontal stripes (only the HUD and menus looked right). With the new frame picture in Diagnostics we found the scene was drawn fine and the game's final upscale was what failed. On Android that step is replaced by a simple upscale of the scene, and the picture is clean.
Ocarina of Time runs about 30 times faster on the phone: that upscale took over 3 seconds a frame on a Pixel 6 Pro, and a frame now takes about a tenth of a second.

Our own fix: on Mali and Adreno phones the emulator allowed less data at once than the phone does, and some GPU programs of Switch 2 games were skipped every frame. It now uses the phone's real limit.
On Android, Ocarina of Time's anti-aliasing defaults to «No sharpening»: the mode that enables the simple upscale.

Satronho NX's own fix: Ocarina of Time closed while loading Hyrule. Ridds' logs showed why: the game keeps data shared between cores at an address that is not aligned, and the phone's processor (ARM) refuses that operation where a PC allows it. The emulator now does it another safe way, and the game ran over 18 minutes without closing.
Satronho NX ships its own FFmpeg for Android with AV1: the videos of Switch 2 games (like Ocarina's scenes) now show. It uses the phone's video decoder and, if that fails, a software one (dav1d).
Our own fix: videos no longer show blocks or lose parts; the emulator waits for the phone's decoder to have room before sending it more.
The memory of Switch 2 games is set up for your phone automatically: no more switches to change. «Free unused memory» was removed, as it could close the game.
The CPU translator uses much less memory for each block of code, and memory stays steady while playing.
Update notice: the app tells you when there is a new Satronho NX build and downloads it from GitHub.

Diagnostics, at the bottom of Suggested settings (off by default): «Count draws per frame» and «Save a picture of a frame». The picture is taken and shared from the in-game menu, to find picture problems on any phone.

builds.titulo: Ocarina of Time boots on the phone

cambios.texto: Satronho NX's own fix: Ocarina of Time closed 15-20 seconds after showing a picture because memory ran out. We tracked it down in Ridds' logs: the CPU translator (Dynarmic) kept some tables for every block of translated code and never freed them, past 1 GB in under a minute. Now they are freed and the translator starts over safely, and the game reaches the logo and the menu.

Our own fix: after a few minutes the game dropped to 1-2 FPS because one of the translator's lists was never emptied and the emulator translated the same code again and again. Now it is emptied, and if the game needs more code at once, the translator keeps more before starting over.

In Switch 2 games the built-in "Max Resolution" and "Texture Pool x2" patches are not applied on the phone (they cost memory and GPU time a phone does not have); "FPS Unlock" still is. The texture cache is capped on phones with 12 GB or less.
Switch 2 games start without precompiling all their shaders at boot (in Ocarina that was over 4 minutes of black screen); shaders are built when they are needed.
The hub opens Switch games with their update and DLC, and if a game does not load, Ñoño tells the real reason.

Memory options at the bottom of Settings → Suggested settings: "Game memory in a file" (recommended for Switch 2) and "Free unused game memory". The log records the phone's memory and why the app last exited, to find problems faster.

builds.titulo: Switch 2 on the phone, step by step

cambios.texto: Satronho NX's own fix: Switch 2 games went black a few seconds in because Android never finished opening the microphone the game asks for at boot (which also kept them from closing). We tracked it down in Ridds' logs, and now the game gets silence, as with the console's microphone muted.

Our own fix: on phones with CPUs older than the Switch 2's, the game's loader crashed under NCE. Satronho NX now uses Dynarmic automatically for Switch 2 games on Android; Switch 1 games keep NCE, which is faster.

"Prepare game" no longer checks, one by one, the compressed files that can never hold shaders: in Ocarina there were almost 186 thousand and they took about 12 minutes on the phone. It also shows its progress, and Stop answers at once.
If a game takes more than 20 seconds to close, Satronho NX restarts itself on the game list instead of freezing.

builds.titulo: In the releases, next to PC

cambios.texto: Switch 2 games on the phone: Satronho NX for Android now reads .nup files, like the PC version (Lichii's Android app doesn't read them yet; we wired this up ourselves). The game shows up in your list with its real version, and its bundled updates and DLC load on their own.

Phone profile for Switch 2: the first time you open a Switch 2 game, Troya offers to give that game alone a lighter internal resolution with FSR and asynchronous shaders, picked for your phone's GPU. If your phone has less than 16 GB of RAM, she warns you before you play.

Phone boost (Suggested settings): Satronho tells Android which threads draw each frame and how long they take, so it raises their speed as soon as a frame runs late and lowers it when the game keeps its pace. On by default, and it can be turned off.

Satronho Emulation (Ridds' hub) now plays your Switch games with Satronho NX: it opens them directly, hands NX your keys and firmware, and when you quit you're back in its library. If the hub installed NX for you, NX adds no icon of its own: it opens from the hub.

Satronho NX for Android now ships in every release, next to the PC version, signed with our key. From this build the app updates itself: when there is a new one, Juana tells you when you open it and it installs on top.
Satronho carousel: the centered game's art shows blurred in the background, and above it go its name, whether it is prepared, its FPS, the time played and the Play and Page buttons.
Back up every save (Settings): all your games' saves in one .zip. That .zip, like each game's, restores in Satronho NX on PC (Ficha Satronho → Restaurar…), and the PC's imports here.
The GPU log is now named satronho_gpu.log too, and the data folder notice says Satronho NX.
Satronho loading screen: the game's art up front, our planet behind and a tip from one of the guides while it loads.
A page for each game (long-press it): time played, sessions, a chart of the last sessions' FPS, and Play, Prepare, Back up saves and Properties in one tap.
Save backup: packs a game's saves into a .zip and shares it to Drive, WhatsApp or your PC.
Satronho capture in the game menu: the picture with a band showing our planet, the game and its FPS, saved and ready to share. Share log is in the menu too.
Game menu with a Satronho header and the session live. Animated start: the planet appears, its ring settles and a little moon goes round.
Style tab: Violet, Night (pure black for OLED screens) and Amber themes; on-screen controls in Satronho violet, classic grey or nearly transparent; and how visible the planet behind the games is.
The phone's temperature in the meter. Past 42 °C, Ñoño tells you in the summary why the FPS dropped and offers a lighter profile.
Ñoño tunes each game: if one is slow two sessions in a row, he offers to lower its resolution just for it, without touching the others.
Continue widget for the home screen: your last game, how it went and a button to keep playing.
The summary when a game closes now shows up (Android went back to the list before it was ready). Games with no shaders to take out ahead, like Celeste, no longer get a ✓ or another offer to prepare.
The Satronho screen, like the desktop window: News, Suggested settings, Ask the guides and Guides, in tabs. Open it from Settings, by long-pressing the bubble or from the app icon.
All five guides with their color, size and topic, as on PC. Each pet can be turned off, and then MechaRidds answers for it.

Summary when a game closes, created by Satronho NX on PC and brought to the phone: how long you played, average FPS and in the slowest moments, stutters and how many came from shaders. If shaders were the problem, Samy offers to prepare the game.
Satronho's mark on each game: ✓ when it is prepared and the FPS of its last session. And the first time you open a game, Samy offers to prepare it.

MechaRidds' three-step welcome (keys, games folder, suggested settings), an Android 13 themed icon with the Satronho planet, the Satronho shortcut on the app icon, and on-screen controls and in-game menu in our colors.
Updates from the app: when a new build is out, Satronho NX tells you, downloads it from the releases and installs it on top. Share log in one tap from the Satronho screen and the summary.
The meter matches the desktop's: Building shaders N · shader stutter. The background logo is now our planet with the guides, as visible as you like (0 to 100 %). Guides and news in English too.

Fixed a crash when opening a game before Android hands over the screen (for example right after rotating the phone or leaving); the log is now satronho_log.txt and shows the build; the AMDBoost effect compiles; and the folder and file-reading errors at startup are gone.
Signed with Satronho NX's own key: uninstall the previous preview once; from here on, everything installs on top.

builds.titulo: The real Satronho NX on Android

cambios.texto: Satronho NX on Android with its own identity: name, logo, notification icon, TV banner, colors and About screen, in every language. The app starts from Eden and Lichii; Satronho NX picked it, adapted it and added everything on this list.
Prepare game, created by Satronho NX and brought to Android from our desktop Prepare for stream: it takes the game's shaders out ahead of time and builds them on the next loading screen.
Suggested settings for your phone: Satronho detects the GPU (Adreno, Mali/Tensor, Xclipse) and the RAM and offers Performance, Balanced and Quality, one recommended, applied in one tap.
The guides come to Android in a floating bubble, with their own knowledge base for the phone. The Satronho meter, the session history, the news and a quick language picker.
